h: A Few Pointers Before You Lean Into the Wind
p: iFLY Milton Keynes sits inside Xscape, the big leisure building in central MK, so there's loads to do under the same roof. That makes it easy to plan a whole day around your flight time without moving the car.

Flying well is mostly about not trying too hard. Beginners tend to stiffen up, kick their legs and flap their arms, which sends them bouncing round the tunnel. Instead, think floppy and calm: chin up, hips forward, slight bend in the knees and arms relaxed. The instructor will use those hand signals to tweak your position, so keep an eye on them rather than the floor.

Empty every pocket, take off rings, watches and earrings, and wear trainers that lace up. Glasses wearers should mention it at check-in. Arrive with time to spare for the training, and maybe save the big meal for afterwards.

Milton Keynes has some brilliant quirks once you've landed. Go hunting for the famous Concrete Cows, a much-loved bit of local public art, or stroll through Campbell Park, which has great views back over the city. Families with younger children often head to Gulliver's Land, a theme park aimed at little ones, while the snow slope inside Xscape is a fun way to cool off. MK's network of redways, the shared paths for walkers and cyclists, makes it easy to explore on foot or by bike, and the city's many parks and lakes are lovely on a fine day.
